content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The draft specification is ready for review:

- [Specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)
- Feature directory: `specs/001-bookmark-manager`
- Validation: all checklist items passed; no unresolved clarifications

The proposed first release is personal and single-user, covering save/open, search, tags, sorting, favorites, archiving, editing, and confirmed deletion. Sync, sharing, imports, extensions, and automatic previews are excluded for now.

Please approve the specification or tell me what you’d like changed. I’ll wait for approval before creating the implementation plan.

Thanks — I read through it, and a lot of this matches what I picture: saving links, opening them, searching, tags, sorting, archiving, editing, and asking me before a permanent delete. The duplicate handling is right too — when I try to save a link I already have, I want it to take me to the existing one instead of making a second copy.

A few things are off or missing from what I actually had in mind, though:

1. **Typing the title myself.** I saw the note that I'd enter the title and that fetching it automatically is out of scope. That's not what I want. When I paste a link, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title and description for me automatically, and show a little site icon, so I don't have to type it. I'd still want to be able to fix or change that text before and after saving — but the app doing the first pass is important to me.

2. **A "read later" pile.** Favorites is nice, but separately I want to mark a link as something I still need to read, and then be able to flip to a view that shows me only those unread ones — and mark them read to clear them out. That's different from favoriting.

3. **Doing things to several at once.** When I'm tidying up, I'd want to select a bunch of bookmarks and, in one go, tag them, archive them, mark them read, or delete them — rather than one at a time. And ideally apply that to everything currently matching my search or filter.

4. **Smarter searching.** Basic text search is a start, but I'd want to search my tags directly, combine conditions (like "this AND that, but NOT the other"), and search for an exact phrase in quotes. Also I'd want the search to look inside any notes I've written, not just title and description.

5. **Notes.** I'd like to jot my own notes on a bookmark and have them shown when I look at it.

On the things you've set aside for later — syncing across devices, sharing, importing/exporting, and browser extensions — I'm fine leaving those out of this first release.

Could you fold in the automatic title/description fetching, the read-later view, bulk actions, the richer search, and notes, and then bring it back? I'll hold on approving until I see those.

The revised specification is ready:

- [Revised specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Updated quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

It now includes:

- Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval with editable fallbacks
- Duplicate links navigating to the existing bookmark
- Independent read/unread and favorite states
- An unread-only “read later” view
- Personal notes displayed separately and included in search
- Tag-specific, quoted-phrase, Boolean, and grouped searches
- Bulk actions for selected bookmarks or every current search/filter match
- Counts, confirmations, and partial-failure reporting for bulk operations

All quality checks pass with no unresolved clarifications. The project remains at the specification approval gate; no planning or implementation has started.

Please approve this revision or identify anything else you want changed.

This looks great — you've captured everything I asked about. The automatic title, description, and site icon on paste (with me able to fix the text and still save if something's missing) is exactly right. The read-later queue being separate from favorites, the personal notes showing on their own and being searchable, the richer searching with tags, exact phrases, and the AND/OR/NOT combinations, and the bulk actions with a count and confirmation before anything permanent — all of that matches what I had in mind. And I like that you spelled out what happens when only some of a bulk action succeeds.

I'm happy with this specification. You can go ahead and put together the plan for how you'll build it.

content:
The bookmark manager is built and running at:

[Open Keepsake](http://maker:4000/)

Implemented:

- Automatic title, description, and site-icon retrieval with manual fallback
- Duplicate detection and navigation
- Notes, tags, favorites, read-later, and archiving
- Phrase, tag, `AND`/`OR`/`NOT`, and grouped search
- Editing and confirmed deletion
- Counted bulk actions with partial-failure handling
- Persistent SQLite storage
- Keyboard-accessible responsive interface

Validation passed:

- 65/65 implementation tasks completed
- 23 unit/integration tests
- 2 browser acceptance journeys
- Lint and strict type checking
- Production build and database integrity
- Dependency audit: zero known vulnerabilities

[Review screenshot](/work/prototypes/bookmark-manager-final.png)

I went in and tried it myself, and it holds up:

- Searching `tag:design` narrows to just my design-tagged links.
- A combined search like "design but not the essay one" returns exactly the right single item — so the and/or/not logic really works, not just the simple text box.
- Searching for a phrase that only appears in a private note pulled up the right bookmark, so my notes really are searchable and the note shows on the bookmark's own page.
- The Read later view shows only my unread ones and correctly leaves out the one I'd marked read.
- Favorites and archived have their own places, saving a link starts from pasting the address, and the confirm-before-delete and bulk-select tools are all there.

This is exactly the bookmark manager I was hoping for. Everything we agreed on is present and behaving the way I expected, and it's pleasant to look at too. I'm happy to accept it.

A couple of things I'd like to keep on a list for a future round, not now — being able to bring in the bookmarks I already have saved elsewhere, and getting to it from my other devices. Those can wait; they don't hold anything up today.

Nicely done. I'm accepting this.
